incidents.cause: The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from terrain while maneuvering at a low altitude.
The pilot's inadvertent hard landing induced by a perceived loss of power and a main transmission anomaly while maneuvering at low altitude.
The pilot's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing. Contributing to the accident was the crosswind.
The flight instructor's delayed remedial action resulting in an off-airfield landing and ground loop.
The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
The pilot’s failure to attain the proper approach path to the runway, resulting in landing short of the runway.
The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard, bounced landing.
The flight instructor's improper flare in gusty wind conditions, which resulted in a hard landing.
The flight instructor's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack during landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and a collision with terrain.
